definition: Merriam-Webster's Word of the Day for November 17, 2026 is: stolid &#149; \STAH-lid\&nbsp; &#149; adjective Stolid describes someone or something that has or expresses little or no emotion. // The detective presented the facts of the case with stolid indifference. See the entry > Examples: "Even the most stolid of personalities can get dragged into drama, breaking one of the biggest rules in journalism: never become the story." — Katie Rosseinsky, The Independent (United Kingdom), 15 Apr. 2026
did_you_know: ? Today, a person described as stolid may simply be someone who doesn't wear their feelings on their sleeve, who appears unemotional or uninterested in what is happening around them. Its use is usually descriptive, rather than disparaging. Once upon a time, however, someone calling you stolid would not be doing you a solid. Stolid comes from the Latin adjective stolidus , meaning "dull" or "stupid." It is also distantly related to the word stultify , meaning "to cause to appear or be stupid, foolish, or absurdly illogical." The earliest examples of usage for stolid , which date back to the 17th century, indicate that it too was originally associated with a lack of smarts; it was used to describe people considered foolish for their relative impassivity. By the 1800s, however, stolid was frequently appearing without such negative connotations, and it continues to be free of such overtones today.
